messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — continuous-batcher queue growth detected in us-west-2. queue_length spike -> sustained. triggering autoscale fallback policy. metric: batcher.queue_len (p95=1200). auto-notify oncall.
sara: I'm oncall, looking. paging into the build logs now, will post quick status.
devon: I'll join in 2m — grabbing handoff. what's current customer impact?
liam: seeing repeated CUDA OOMs in runtime logs around the same time as queue growth. snippet below from runtime logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:04:33Z ERROR runtime/worker.go:412 worker=vm-23 cuda: out of memory while allocating 256MB
2026-03-15T12:04:34Z WARN batcher/queue.go:198 queue_size=342 -> 1200 growth_rate=3.5x
2026-03-15T12:04:35Z ERROR runtime/handler.go:88 container crash: signal SIGABRT
```
jun: batcher pods are crashlooping on a subset of nodes, GPU mem pressure high. noticed a single model variant (gptx-8q) has unusually high per-request KV size; looks correlated.
sara: quick mitigation options: 1) disable continuous growth (set BATCHER_MAX_SIZE=128) 2) route traffic away from affected model variant -> smaller quantized model 3) throttle ingress for partner customers.
liam: I ran `kubectl describe pod batcher-xyz -n redwood` — events show OOMKilled and kubelet evicting other pods. nodes with highest pressure: ip-10-0-4-22, ip-10-0-4-23.
```
Name: batcher-xyz
Status: CrashLoopBackOff
Last State: Terminated
  Reason: OOMKilled
  Exit Code: 137
```
karen: I'm creating a customer-impact ticket for accounts team (cust-479, cust-882 reported elevated latency/5xx). tagging @accounts-escalations.
devon: taking this oncall. immediate plan: 1) pin limiter to 100 req/s for the model route, 2) run rolling restart of batcher deployment with BATCH_MAX_BATCH=64 (non-disruptive targeting), 3) activate fallback routing to small-model-quant.
liam: +1 on rolling restart; also recommend enabling kernel-level cgroup mem limits to avoid node-wide evictions while we stabilize.
sara: I'm going to flip a conservative throttle on the route: `redwood route update --name chat-gptx --rate-limit 100` (doing now). will monitor.
jun: FYI, tracing shows backlog is dominated by long-lived requests from one customer job — looks like a misconfigured heavy-batch client. IP and keys in support ticket.
amsg: (support bot) created ticket #INC-2026-331, assigned to accounts-escalations.
pagerduty: Incident declared SEV-2. Pager duty schedule paged for oncall escalation.
karen: opening high-priority support channel + notifying affected customers with short note: "We're aware of elevated latency and are actively mitigating. We'll share updates in 15 minutes."
devon: executing rolling restart with new envs now. command: `kubectl set env deployment/batcher BATCH_MAX_BATCH=64 BATCH_MEMORY_LIMIT=1Gi -n redwood && kubectl rollout restart deployment/batcher -n redwood`
(rolling restart started)
sara: observed immediate drop in queue length from 1200 -> 220 after throttle applied. latency p95 down from 11s -> 3.8s. still seeing a handful of OOMs during restart.
liam: digging into kernel OOM logs — looks like a particular node suffered cgroup misconfiguration, failing to reclaim. I've cordoned ip-10-0-4-23 and draining it to stop evictions.
jun: while we drain, we should toggle routing policy to prefer nodes with dedicated-gpu-pool tag, to reduce cross-tenant interference.
devon: switched route to dedicated pool for critical customers, and enabled fallback to small-model-quant for noncritical. traffic rebalanced.
sara: customer update sent. still monitoring for 10m before closing the active incident.
karen: accounting: two customers reported 502/timeout spikes; ops will follow up for credits if SLA hit.
liam: postmortem items so far — investigate continuous-batcher growth trigger, add per-model KV size caps, improve node-level cgroup defaults, add route-level automatic degradation to quantized variants.
devon: handoff note: devon taking over active mitigation and timeline. I'll keep this thread updated. Sara handing off at 12:10 UTC.
sara: handing over to @devon — all current mitigations: route throttle applied, batcher MAX set to 64, dedicated pool routing on for critical, node ip-10-0-4-23 cordoned/draining.
devon: ack. next steps — finish drain, watch OOM events for 15m, if stable we can revert conservative throttles gradually. will open postmortem ticket and include customer-impact windows.
liam: ping me if OOMs reappear, I'll prepare node repro and attach memory heap/profile.
karen: I'll draft the customer incident summary and coordinate support. thanks all for quick reaction. :thumbsup: 
(incident-bot): note — incident created INC-2026-331, severity=SEV-2, runbook used: continuous-batcher-throttle.
